exercise.name: Bridge Hip Abduction
aliases: Glute bridge hold with knee outs

reference.title: Bridge Hip Abduction
reference.listing: Video (movement reference; the page could not be read at authoring time: gymvisual.com is blocked by the proxy, so the movement comes from the name and standard coaching practice)

exercise.mechanics: Compound (hip extension held; hip abduction with external rotation at the top)

breathing.pattern: Breathe out as the hips rise, breathe steadily through the knee openings, breathe in as you lower.
breathing.cadence: About 1.5 s up, two open-close reps of about 1.6 s, 2 s down

prescription.tempo: Hips up in about 1.5 s, knees open and close in about 1.5 s, lower in 2 s
prescription.progression: More openings per bridge, then a mini band around the knees, then single-leg bridges.

cues.text: Lie on your back, knees bent, feet flat and hip width, arms on the floor by your sides.
Breathe out and push through the heels to lift the hips until knees, hips and shoulders line up.
Keep the hips high and level, then open both knees out to the sides and bring them back together.
Breathe in and roll the hips down slowly.

mistakes.mistake: Hips sagging while the knees open
mistakes.fix: Squeeze the glutes and keep the hips at the height of the bridge.

mistakes.mistake: Arching the low back at the top
mistakes.fix: Ribs down; stop when knees, hips and shoulders form a line.
Keep the feet planted; let them roll only onto their outer edges.
Open and close under control, about a second each way.

kinematics.norm: Hips extended to neutral at the top, knee-hip-shoulder line straight (Lehecka 2017)
Knees open outward with the feet fixed: hip abduction with external rotation; side-lying and clam-type abduction work loads gluteus medius (Selkowitz 2013, Boren 2011)
Stay planted, rolling onto the outer edges (clinical opinion)
Controlled, about 1-2 s per movement (clinical opinion)

sources.title: GymVisual #989, Bridge Hip Abduction, video (movement reference)
Lehecka et al. 2017, building a better gluteal bridge: EMG of hip muscles during modified single-leg bridges (Int J Sports Phys Ther 12(4):543-549; PMC5534144)
Macadam and Feser 2019, gluteus maximus EMG excitation during dynamic body-weight hip extension: a systematic review (Int J Sports Phys Ther 14(1):14-31; PMC6350668)

Selkowitz, Beneck & Powers 2013, which exercises target the gluteal muscles while minimizing activation of the tensor fascia lata? Fine-wire EMG of 11 exercises (J Orthop Sports Phys Ther 43(2):54-64)
Boren et al. 2011, EMG analysis of gluteus medius and gluteus maximus during rehabilitation exercises (Int J Sports Phys Ther 6(3):206-223; PMC3201064)

cautions: Stop if sharp pain, numbness or giving-way occurs.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
Low-back discomfort at the top usually means arching: lift a little less and tuck the pelvis.
Hamstring cramping: move the feet a little closer to the hips.
modify: Hip or groin discomfort: open the knees less.

muscleNotes.glute_max_r: Holds the hips extended in the bridge; its upper fibres also help open the knee (Macadam 2019).
muscleNotes.glute_max_l: Holds the hips extended in the bridge; its upper fibres also help open the knee (Macadam 2019).
muscleNotes.glute_med_r: Abducts and rotates the thigh outward to open the knee (Selkowitz 2013).
muscleNotes.glute_med_l: Abducts and rotates the thigh outward to open the knee (Selkowitz 2013).
muscleNotes.hamstrings_r: Assist hip extension in the bridge (Lehecka 2017).
muscleNotes.hamstrings_l: Assist hip extension in the bridge (Lehecka 2017).
muscleNotes.core: Keeps the pelvis level and the ribs down (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.spinal_extensors_r: Hold the trunk line in the bridge (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.spinal_extensors_l: Hold the trunk line in the bridge (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.adductors_r: Control the knees back together (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.adductors_l: Control the knees back together (clinical opinion).
